## Installation

You can install the development version of tRc from [GitHub](https://github.com/) with:

``` r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("TamakiRegen/trc")
```

## Date to FY Quarter

Takes a date object and returns either the financial year, year and quarter, or quarter that the date falls in.

```{r fy_example}
library(trc)

date <- "2026-05-30"

trc::d2fyq(date, type = "year")
trc::d2fyq(date, type = "year_quarter")
trc::d2fyq(date, type = "quarter")
```

## Tamaki SA2 Filter

Filter a vector of StatsNZ Census 2023 SA2 codes to only include those that cover the Tamaki Regeneration area.

Note that the `col` parameter must be parsed into the function as a string.

```{r sa2_example}
library(trc)

# Create the Tāmaki and New Zealand SA2 dataset
codes <- data.frame(
  SA22026_code = c(
    147001, 144700, 191201, 146700, 338200, 221500, 243200, 145800, 
    400013, 146301, 214500, 362100, 115100, 145400, 147100, 147002, 
    132501, 243800, 146302
  ),
  SA22026_name = c(
    "Tamaki West", "Glen Innes West", "Te Puna", "Panmure West", 
    "Tinwald South", "Ohangai", "Maungaraki", "Glen Innes East-Wai O Taiki Bay", 
    "Snares Islands", "Point England North", "Nelson Park", "Georgetown", 
    "Stanmore Bay East", "Panmure Glen Innes Industrial", "Panmure East", 
    "Tamaki East", "Konini Road", "Tirohanga", "Point England South"
  )
)

print(codes)

filtered_sa2 <- trc::sa2(codes, "SA22026_code")

print(filtered_sa2)
```

## Save and Load Timestamped Files

Create version controlled, timestamped files when exporting data from R (then load them again without writing out timestamps each time).

These function relies on the `rio()` package, which supports multiple formats [listed here](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/rio/vignettes/rio.html). However, the package won't support the `rio()` functionality of exporting two R objects as separate sheets in the same workbook (for that you'll need a more manual workaround).

### Saving files
Example of `save_timestamped_file()`:
```
trc::save_timestamped_file(df, "clean_data", sub_dir = "outputs", "xlsx")

outputs/20260530_172534_clean_data.xlsx
```
Note that the `sub_dir` parameter defaults to `NULL`, and will therefore save the file into the working directory if not defined.

### Loading files
While great for version control, timestamped files like the example above are a bitch to load. Most of the time you just want to have the most recent file loaded into a script. The `load_timestamped_file()`function will take the target filename and extension and search the target directory for the latest timestamp (of the format `YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS`) before loading it.

## Rehousing Matrix
This function takes the [Rehousing Matrix](https://github.com/TamakiRegen/rh_matrix) and applies it to a value.

 - Rows with >=6 bedrooms are not treated by the matrix and will return the same number of bedrooms as the input number. This is due to a limit of both rehousing data to calculate distributions, and the low number of these large properties in our portfolio.
 - Rows with zero bedrooms return zero as there is no rehousing demand. This is likely to be either an untenantable house (e.g. fire damage) or a SPM land entry has crept into the data you're trying to mutate. In either case, zero bedroom values should be investigated.
 - Be sure to filter !is.na(current) in your dataframe before applying the matrix.

 ```{r rh_demo}
library(trc)

rehousing_data <- data.frame(
  address = c('1 Big John Street', '2 Big John Street', '3 Big John Street', '4 Big John Street',
  '5 Big John Street', '6 Big John Street', '1 Extra Medium John Place', '3 Extra Medium John Place'),
  current_bedrooms = c(2,3,3,4,1,7,0,5)
)

rehousing_data <- rehousing_data %>% 
  mutate(required_bedrooms = trc::rh_matrix(current_bedrooms))

print(rehousing_data)

 ```

### Other things to note
 - The results will be different each time you run it as the function takes a sample based on the observed distribution of bedroom typology shifts.
 - The code doesn't know the exact circumstances of the whanau in each home, and therefore provides an **indicative best guess** at what bedroom typologies will be required.
 - Because of this, the **outputs are for planning purposes only, and need to be validated with THA before being operationalised.**

 ## Hex Codes
 This offers a quick way of printing TRC brand colour hex codes in the console. These can then be copied into `ase()`arguments for visualisations.

 The library defaults to TRC's standard colours, but the parameter "light" can be entered to get a lighter shade of each of the five brand colours.

 ```{r hex_demo}
 library(trc)
 
 trc::hex()

 trc::hex("light")
 ```
